value.reason: The field at models/user.ts:97-100 (redacted, but the data-flow notes tie it to deluxeToken) is set up as a plain `DataTypes.STRING` with `defaultValue: ''`. The excerpt shows no `set()` hook, no encryption and no hashing. This matches the positive example (a plain typed field) and not the negative one (a setter that encrypts the value). Two confirmed write paths store this authentication secret without any transform: `UserModel.create` in data/datacreator.ts:192-201 writes `security.deluxeToken(completeEmail)`, and `user.update` in routes/deluxe.ts:43 writes the deluxe token. The data goes to a SQLite file (`data/juiceshop.sqlite`, models/index.ts:42) that sits on EFS (terraform/main.tf:64). EFS at-rest encryption only depends on `var.efs_encrypted`, whose value isn't in the evidence, so storage-level protection is unconfirmed. Either way, disk encryption wouldn't stop the token being read in plaintext by anyone with database access. The sensitive value is stored without app-level encryption, hashing or tokenisation.
